elements.text: IEC 61508 is the governing functional safety standard; integrity is allocated as a required Safety Integrity Level per actor. SIL 0 means no safety requirement.
The required SIL of every actor is an input from a hazard and risk analysis outside this argument.

Pattern catalog patterns.yaml: structure, placement relations, SIL range and covered fault classes of each pattern, after Armoush, Koopman. Every pattern choice and placement rule in this argument rests on it.
Platform: 28 core slots across 10 fault containment regions, core types cortexM, cortexR, ppcE200. Cores actually instantiated in this solution: [1, 2, 7, 13, 14].
Applications: c_rasta, modelled as synchronous dataflow graphs and unfolded to an equivalent homogeneous graph before mapping.

Fault model under consideration: random hardware faults and systematic software faults. Patterns not covering this fault class were excluded from the design space, and placement relations motivated only by an excluded fault class were not posted. Systematic faults are covered only as far as they differ between core types and toolchains, or between a doer and a checker with a different algorithm; design faults common to diverse implementations need diverse development. Not addressed: transient faults, timing and omission faults, faults of the interconnect, latent faults, diagnostic coverage, and degraded modes.

This argument is generated from a design space exploration result. It argues only over properties of the ARCHITECTURE and its DEPLOYMENT: which pattern is applied to which actor, where components are placed relative to each other, how integrity levels are provisioned per core, and whether the resulting schedule meets its timing requirement. Claims about implementation correctness, detection coverage and development process are outside what a mapping can establish and are carried below as undeveloped goals. The SIL range of a pattern is a precondition taken from the catalog, necessary but not sufficient for a SIL: this argument computes no failure rates, hardware fault tolerance, safe failure fraction or diagnostic coverage.

The worst-case execution times supplied to the exploration are sound upper bounds for every actor on every core type it may be bound to. The exploration consumes these figures; it does not establish them.

Token preservation: every replica fires on every iteration and produces on all of its outputs, in the fault-free and in the degraded case alike. Detection marks a token invalid; it never withholds one. The timing argument therefore holds in the degraded mode, at the cost of being conservative when no fault is present.

The verifier re-checks the solution against the instance produced by the front end, not against the original specification. The instance represents the platform, execution times, pattern catalog and safety requirements correctly; an error in the front end or in the specification would be common to the exploration and the verifier.
The deployed architecture of f_both3 meets, for every safety-related actor, the architectural preconditions that the pattern catalog states for the actor's required SIL.

Pattern two_of_two_high_sil [koopman, Two Channel (2-of-2)]: Two channels, both at high SIL, compute the same function and must agree. Channel b receives the owner's result, compares it with its own, and returns the verdict to the owner over an edge with one initial token; on a disagreement the owner marks its output invalid and the pair goes to its safe state (fails silent), so the fault reaction starts within one iteration. No explicit voter: 2-of-2 requires agreement rather than a majority, so the comparison folds into channel b and the owner, and no explicit voter is needed. The name is Koopman's; it is not IEC 61508 MooN notation. Both channels always fire and always produce, per the token-preservation obligation. A detected disagreement marks the token invalid; it never withholds it. So the timing guarantee holds in the degraded mode too, at the price of being conservative in the fault-free case. Attainable SIL [3, 4]; covers random_hw, systematic_sw; fails silent; voter folded.
A fault in either channel is detected as a disagreement between the two channels. [two_of_two_high_sil/SC1]
Achieved through the Comparison tactic (Checking): Detection of discrepancies of redundant system outputs.
Comparison: Tests whether the outputs of fully redundant subsystems are equal in order to detect failures. Usually implies the use of a redundancy tactic.
Candidate methods from the standard: IEC 61508-7 A.1.3 comparator; IEC 61508-7 A.6.5 input comparison/voting
An IEC 61508 method realising Comparison is implemented in frontEnd, and its effectiveness for the faults of concern is demonstrated.

Pattern low_sil_diverse_doer_checker [koopman, Low SIL Doer/Checker Pair, armoush, HtD]: low_sil_doer_checker with the checker additionally required to be a DIVERSE implementation on a different processor type. Added because the encoded Koopman catalogue has a hole: at SIL 2 the separated pair defends against random hardware faults and the co-located pair against systematic software faults, but nothing covers BOTH. Separation alone does not help against a systematic fault, since an identical checker on another core reproduces the same mistake. The cost is Armoush's heterogeneous-duplex figure: two independent developments, roughly 200% of one, against ~100% for an identical copy. Attainable SIL [1, 2]; covers random_hw, systematic_sw; fails active; voter folded.
An implausible output of the doer is detected by the checker. [low_sil_diverse_doer_checker/SC1]
Achieved through the Sanity Check tactic (Checking): Detection of implausible system outputs or states.

Sanity Check: Checks whether a system state or value remains within a valid range which can be defined in the system specification or which is based on knowledge about the internal structure or nature of the system.

elements.text: No core hosts software of differing integrity without certified partitioning, and every core is provisioned to at least the highest integrity level it hosts.

Koopman's rule 2: absent certified partitioning, all software on a processor must be developed to the highest integrity level present on it. Whether a core type can provide such partitioning is declared per core type by the platform.

Software on different cores does not interfere except through the interconnect; shared memory, caches and input/output are not modelled, so applying the rule per core assumes freedom from interference between cores. Certified partitioning, where used, separates software of different SIL on one core in space and time.
Achieved through the Barrier tactic (Isolation): protect a subsystem from influences of other subsystems.
Independent re-check of the solution: all 28 core slots re-examined against their type ceiling and against the set of integrity levels actually hosted.
The deployed mapping and static order meet the declared timing requirements, in the fault-free and in the degraded case alike.
Iteration period per application: [1130]. Timing is a safety property here because a replica that misses its deadline cannot perform the check the pattern credits it with.

Independent re-check of the solution: the mapping- and scheduling-aware graph was rebuilt from the returned assignment and its period computed twice by disjoint methods -- Lawler's parametric maximum-cycle-ratio search and max-plus self-timed simulation -- which agree with each other, and the period the solver reported is the least integer at or above that ratio.
Independent re-check of the solution: the reported period is at least the total execution demand of the busiest core, the bound that a static order left open as a chain silently loses.
Every detected fault brings the function to its safe state within the process safety time.
elements.note: fault reaction and process safety time are not modelled

elements.text: In the dataflow model, a component's verdict on iteration k reaches the owner over an edge with t initial tokens, i.e. in the owner's firing t iterations later (low_sil_diverse_doer_checker: t = 1, two_of_two_high_sil: t = 1). The reaction itself and the process safety time are not modelled.
Every software component is developed, verified and validated to its required safety integrity level in accordance with IEC 61508-3.

elements.text: Integrity levels to be discharged by process, as active component counts: SIL 1: 4, SIL 2: 2, SIL 3: 4. Components implemented above their required level were promoted to satisfy Koopman's rule 2; the cost of that promotion is what the exploration minimised.
